dossier.purpose: OpenAI's catalog of Agent Skills for Codex; the README says the repository is deprecated in favour of github.com/openai/plugins (README.md:2). At commit 49f948f it holds 44 skill folders: 5 in skills/.system (imagegen, openai-docs, plugin-creator, skill-creator, skill-installer) and 39 in skills/.curated. Each skill is a SKILL.md (YAML name + description frontmatter, Markdown procedure) plus agents/openai.yaml (Codex UI and MCP-dependency metadata) and optional scripts/, references/, assets/. Engineering and security content: security-best-practices (Python, JS/TS, Go reference files), security-threat-model, security-ownership-map (git-history ownership and bus-factor scripts), gh-fix-ci, gh-address-comments, yeet, cli-creator, define-goal, playwright and playwright-interactive, screenshot, pdf, jupyter-notebook, aspnet-core, winui-app, sentry. The rest are deploy skills (vercel, netlify, cloudflare, render), connector skills (8 figma*, 4 notion-*, linear) and OpenAI-product skills (openai-docs, chatgpt-apps, imagegen, speech, transcribe, migrate-to-codex). It is content (Markdown plus helper scripts), not a framework. It contains no evaluation runner or scorer framework, no containerized Claude Code/Codex end-to-end runner, and no CI regression gate. The only evaluation artifacts are 8 manual-run JSON scenarios under four Notion skills.

claims.claim: 'This repository is deprecated. For current Codex skill and plugin examples, use the OpenAI Plugins repository' (github.com/openai/plugins); to add your own skills follow the Build plugins guide, which covers creating a skill-only plugin.
'Agent Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that AI agents can discover and use to perform at specific tasks. Write once, use everywhere.'

'Codex uses skills to help package capabilities that teams and individuals can use to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way. This repository catalogs skills for use and distribution with Codex.'
Links to Codex skills docs and to the 'Agent Skills open standard' (agentskills.io).
'Skills in .system are automatically installed in the latest version of Codex.'
'To install curated or experimental skills, you can use the $skill-installer inside Codex.'
Curated skills can be installed by name (defaults to skills/.curated), e.g. '$skill-installer gh-address-comments'.

Experimental skills are installed by naming the folder (create-plan from .experimental) or by giving the GitHub directory URL https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.experimental/create-plan.
'After installing a skill, restart Codex to pick up new skills.'
'The license of an individual skill can be found directly inside the skill's directory inside the LICENSE.txt file.'
Security contact: 'Have you discovered a vulnerability or have concerns about model output? Please e-mail security@openai.com'.
The README (43 lines) is silent on Claude Code, evaluation or testing, CI, supported operating systems, telemetry and benchmarks.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or phone-home code found: every outbound HTTP use in skills/**/scripts was enumerated and none is analytics. Network use is per skill and explicit. (1) skill-installer calls api.github.com for listing, codeload.github.com zip download, and git clone fallback over HTTPS then SSH (github_utils.py:21; install-skill-from-github.py:81,128-161,187-206); requests carry User-Agent codex-skill-install or codex-skill-list (github_utils.py:11; install-skill-from-github.py:56; list-skills.py:31) and attach GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN as an Authorization header when set (github_utils.py:12-14); SKILL.md says the scripts need network and sandbox escalation (skill-installer/SKILL.md:34). (2) openai-docs helper fetches https://developers.openai.com/codex/codex-manual.md with User-Agent codex-openai-docs, checks an x-content-sha256 header and caches under a temp dir (skills/.system/openai-docs/scripts/fetch-codex-manual.mjs:19-24,34,461-469); resolve-latest-model-info.js fetches the latest-model guide (:7-8,39-40). (3) vercel-deploy fallback uploads a project tarball without authentication to https://codex-deploy-skills.vercel.sh/api/deploy (skills/.curated/vercel-deploy/scripts/deploy.sh:9,239). (4) playwright wrapper runs 'npx --yes --package @playwright/cli' (playwright/scripts/playwright_cli.sh:19), so it hits the npm registry. Accounts and credentials needed per skill: OPENAI_API_KEY (imagegen CLI fallback, imagegen/SKILL.md:15; speech/SKILL.md:3; transcribe), gh auth (gh-fix-ci/SKILL.md:14; gh-address-comments/SKILL.md:12; yeet/SKILL.md:8-9), Sentry login or token (sentry/SKILL.md:11,19-20), Render API key or OAuth (render-deploy/SKILL.md:121,203), Netlify and Cloudflare OAuth (netlify-deploy/SKILL.md:35,58; cloudflare-deploy/SKILL.md:24), Notion and Linear MCP OAuth via 'codex mcp login' (notion-knowledge-capture/SKILL.md:25-26; linear/SKILL.md:30-31), Figma MCP. security-best-practices, security-threat-model and security-ownership-map need no account (ownership-map needs Python and networkx); security-best-practices only optionally suggests searching online (security-best-practices/SKILL.md:24).

code.architecture: Content repository with no shared library code. Layout: skills/.system/<skill>/ (5 skills) and skills/.curated/<skill>/ (39 skills); 780 files under skills/ (739 curated, 41 system). Each skill dir has SKILL.md, agents/openai.yaml (interface block, optional dependencies.tools MCP entries, optional policy.allow_implicit_invocation, set only in chatgpt-apps/agents/openai.yaml:12-13) and LICENSE, plus optional scripts/, references/, assets/, and evaluations/ (4 Notion skills only). Loading model per skill-creator/SKILL.md:71-72,127-133: only name and description are read to decide triggering, the body loads after trigger, bundled references load as needed. Selective loading is spelled out for the security skills: security-best-practices picks reference files by language and framework using the <language>-<framework>-<stack>-security.md naming (SKILL.md:18,37), and security-threat-model says 'Only load the reference files you need' (SKILL.md:81). Key modules: skill-installer (github_utils.py, install-skill-from-github.py with path-traversal-checked unzip at :105-112, list-skills.py); skill-creator (init_skill.py, generate_openai_yaml.py, quick_validate.py); plugin-creator (create_basic_plugin.py); migrate-to-codex (scripts/cli.py coordinator, scripts/migrate/{instructions,skills,agents,mcps,hooks,plugins,settings,codex_config,common}.py, scripts/utils/{scan,util}.py); security-ownership-map/scripts (4 Python files, 2,183 lines); security-best-practices/references (10 files, 8,957 lines: python-django/fastapi/flask, javascript express/nextjs/react/vue/jquery/general-frontend, golang-general-backend); security-threat-model/references (prompt-template.md, security-controls-and-assets.md). Skill bodies total 8,294 lines across 44 SKILL.md files.

claim_checks.evidence: All 44 skill dirs share the SKILL.md layout with name/description frontmatter, and no skill uses frontmatter keys outside name, description and metadata (skills/.system/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py:40 lists the allowed keys). But distribution and runtime are Codex-specific: installer default destination is $CODEX_HOME/skills (skills/.system/skill-installer/scripts/install-skill-from-github.py:45-46,243-244); agents/openai.yaml is described as 'product-specific config' (skills/.system/skill-creator/references/openai_yaml.md:3); 21 of 44 SKILL.md files contain Codex-only strings such as js_repl, sandbox_permissions=require_escalated, CODEX_HOME, $skill-installer or .codex/ (e.g. skills/.curated/gh-address-comments/SKILL.md:12, playwright/SKILL.md:37-41, playwright-interactive/SKILL.md:3). The three security skills, gh-fix-ci and yeet contain none of those strings. No Claude Code install or loading path is documented; Claude Code is only a migration source (migrate-to-codex/SKILL.md:10, references/differences.md:5).

risks: Maintenance: the README declares the repository deprecated in favour of github.com/openai/plugins (README.md:2), and it still documents a skills/.experimental folder that does not exist at this commit (README.md:27-37), so the documented tree and the real tree already diverge.

Codex-only design with no documented Claude Code path: install target is $CODEX_HOME/skills (install-skill-from-github.py:45-46,243-244), agents/openai.yaml is a Codex-specific schema (skill-creator/references/openai_yaml.md:3), and 21 of 44 SKILL.md files contain Codex-only strings (skills/.curated/gh-address-comments/SKILL.md:12; playwright/SKILL.md:37-41; playwright-interactive/SKILL.md:3). Claude Code appears only as a migration source (migrate-to-codex/SKILL.md:10). Whether Claude Code loads these skills per task is not stated anywhere in the repo.

No quality gate in the repo: no tests, no CI workflows (.github absent), no lint or pre-commit config, no release automation and no SECURITY.md. The only evaluation artifacts are 8 manual-run JSON scenarios with no runner or scorer (notion-*/evaluations/README.md:38-45) that name skills which do not exist (conversation-to-wiki.json:3; status-meeting-prep.json:3). The repo provides no labeled-case scorer framework, no containerized Claude Code/Codex end-to-end runner and no declarative CI regression gate.

Unpinned and unverified distribution: the installer downloads the default-branch archive (DEFAULT_REF 'main', install-skill-from-github.py:18,80-96) with no commit pin, checksum or signature, and refuses to overwrite an existing skill directory (:290-291), so there is no in-tool update path. Runtime fetches are also unpinned: 'npx --yes --package @playwright/cli' (playwright/scripts/playwright_cli.sh:19) and 'npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest' (playwright/SKILL.md:28).

Data egress: the no-auth fallback of vercel-deploy tars the project, excluding only node_modules, .git, .env and .env.*, and POSTs it to https://codex-deploy-skills.vercel.sh/api/deploy (skills/.curated/vercel-deploy/scripts/deploy.sh:9,201-206,239). Its SKILL.md does not warn that source is uploaded to a third party (vercel-deploy/SKILL.md:33-52).

Mixed licensing with no repo-level license: 8 Figma skills fall under proprietary Figma Developer Terms offered as a revocable Beta (skills/.curated/figma/LICENSE.txt:1-2); 5 are MIT (notion-* x4, vercel-deploy); 31 are Apache-2.0, 29 of them with the unfilled copyright appendix (e.g. skills/.system/skill-creator/LICENSE.txt:190); the playwright skills derive from microsoft/playwright-cli (playwright/NOTICE.txt:1-14); license file names are inconsistent (LICENSE.TXT x6, in 6 of the 8 Figma skills).
